scope: Resolve the sendlogreceiver-demux pass's open question: chat-render helper consolidation. Plan hypothesized 16 UI/text-render helpers shared across PrivateChat / PartyChat / LinkshellChat receivers. INVESTIGATION RESULT: separate Chat*Receiver classes DON'T EXIST in this codebase - chat is on the World channel (live capture deferred). Pivoted to (a) catalog the 3 named-but-uncataloged render helpers from BCS-Y-0251 SendLogReceiver apply notes, (b) document the architectural absence of Chat*Receiver classes, (c) flag the broader shared chat-render pipeline.

method.step1: Search symbols.json for PrivateChat / PartyChat / LinkshellChat receivers. Found only c2s BCS-Y-0309 ChatOutbound_PartyChat_emitter_FUN_004DF6D0. NO s2c Chat*Receiver classes cataloged.
method.step2: Cross-check receiver_opcode_map_inbound.json + client_receivers.json for chat-related receivers. None found.
method.step3: Confirm via reference-pcap-corpus memory: 54 unencrypted pcaps are MAP CHANNEL only. PartyChat / LinkshellChat / PrivateChat run on the World channel which is outside the captured corpus.
method.step4: Decomp the 3 named uncataloged helpers (FUN_0076F5A0 / FUN_007906C0 / FUN_00778D50) from BCS-Y-0251 SendLogReceiver apply notes.
method.step5: Per-helper findings: FUN_0076F5A0 (115B, 3 callers): generic zero-init helper for 9-field state struct. FUN_007906C0 (800B, 7 callers): SHARED chat-render text-parser state machine - byte-stream walker with 7+ cases dispatching to vtable on param_2 renderer interface. FUN_00778D50 (45B, 2 callers): typed-cast guard (throws bad_cast if validation byte set).
method.step6: Cross-callers of FUN_007906C0 reveal SHARED chat-render pipeline: 7 callers including FUN_0089fbf0 (SendLogReceiver::apply BCS-Y-0251), FUN_0089eb40 (UNCATALOGED - sibling receiver apply), FUN_0089e320 (UNCATALOGED - sibling receiver apply), plus 4 sibling wrappers FUN_00790aa0/b20/a30/ba0. The two uncataloged 0x0089xxxx callers are likely other Lua-side text-rendering receivers (could be SystemMessage* or NoticeMessage* family). Flagged for future investigation.

key_findings: REVISED sendlogreceiver-demux-pass result: PrivateChat / PartyChat / LinkshellChat receivers DO NOT EXIST as cataloged Receiver classes. These opcodes live on the World channel (out of scope for the 54-capture Map-channel pcap corpus). The chat-render helper consolidation hypothesis applies only to MAP-CHANNEL chat (SendLogReceiver = GameMessage* family + the 2 uncataloged 0x0089xxxx sibling receivers).

FUN_007906C0 is the SHARED CHAT-RENDER TEXT-PARSER (800B). 7 callers prove cross-receiver sharing: FUN_0089fbf0 (SendLogReceiver::apply BCS-Y-0251) + FUN_0089eb40 (uncataloged sibling) + FUN_0089e320 (uncataloged sibling) + 4 sibling wrappers FUN_00790aa0/b20/a30/ba0. Byte-stream walker with 7+ cases dispatching to vtable slots on param_2 renderer interface. This is the architectural 'shared render surface' the sendlogreceiver-demux pass hypothesized - just located via parser-sharing rather than receiver-sharing.

FUN_0076F5A0 (115B) is a generic zero-init helper for a 9-field state struct (+4/+8/+0xc/+0x10/+0x18/+0x1c/+0x20/+0x24/+0x28). 3 callers: SendLogReceiver::apply + FUN_00712dd0 + FUN_006ed2d0. NOT chat-specific - it's a general state-reset utility used by multiple subsystems.

FUN_00778D50 (45B) is a typed-cast guard helper. Throws std::bad_cast if param_1+8 byte != 0, otherwise returns *(param_1+4). 2 callers: SendLogReceiver::apply + FUN_00cb2d50. Used for safe pointer extraction after dynamic_cast.

Discovery items: 2 uncataloged Lua-side sibling receivers (FUN_0089EB40 and FUN_0089E320) share the chat-render pipeline with SendLogReceiver via FUN_007906C0. Likely names: SystemMessageReceiver, NoticeMessageReceiver, or similar Map-channel notification receivers. Flagged for future receiver-class hunting (candidate).

Architectural finding: in this 1.x client, chat receivers are routed by the LuaActorImpl::vftable[N] dispatch mechanism (per the 0x16b-0x16c-dual-path-resolution pass finding). For PartyChat / LinkshellChat / PrivateChat (World channel), the receivers exist but would be hosted on a different actor type than CharaElement - which means they're outside FUN_0058CCA0's case table and outside this codebase's Map-channel-only attribution scope. The live-capture deferral means these can't be characterized statically without live capture against the World channel.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: Chat_SharedTextParser_FUN_007906C0
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: 800-byte SHARED chat-render text-parser state machine. Byte-stream walker that switches on byte value (cases 0-7+ with default 0xFF) and per-case dispatches to vtable slots on param_2 renderer interface. Cases 0-1: FUN_00791cf0 prefix-parse + vtable[2/3] dispatch. Case 2: std_string ctor + null-terminated string scan + vtable[4] dispatch. Cases 3-4: 1-byte read + vtable[1] dispatch. Case 5: marker (no payload) + vtable[11]. Case 6: vtable[5] with parsed prefix. Case 7+: complex multi-field paths. 7 CALLERS proving cross-receiver sharing: [[SendLogReceiver::apply_FUN_0089FBF0]] (BCS-Y-0251), FUN_0089EB40 (uncataloged sibling receiver), FUN_0089E320 (uncataloged sibling receiver), FUN_00790aa0/b20/a30/ba0 (sibling wrappers). This architectural finding: the 'shared chat-render surface' the sendlogreceiver-demux pass hypothesized exists here, accessible to any Map-channel text-rendering receiver. World-channel chat receivers (PrivateChat/PartyChat/LinkshellChat) likely use the same parser via the same vtable-dispatch pattern but are outside this codebase's scope (live capture deferred).

SEH-protected with FUN_00cc9310 sub-cleanup. 3 callers: [[SendLogReceiver::apply_FUN_0089FBF0]] (BCS-Y-0251), FUN_00712dd0, FUN_006ed2d0. proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: Chat_TypedCastGuard_FUN_00778D50
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: 45-byte typed-cast guard helper. Throws std::bad_cast if *(param_1+8) byte is non-zero, otherwise returns *(param_1+4). 2 callers: [[SendLogReceiver::apply_FUN_0089FBF0]] (BCS-Y-0251), FUN_00cb2d50. Used to safely extract a typed pointer from a result wrapper that carries a 'validation failed' flag at byte+8 - if flag is set, the dynamic_cast that produced the wrapper failed, so accessing the pointer at +4 would be invalid and we throw bad_cast.
